CausalChain: HCC tumor → Elevated PCSK9 expression → Increased degradation of LDLR on T cells → Impaired TCR recycling and signaling → Reduced CD8+ T cell activation → Suboptimal response to PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors → Inhibition of PCSK9 restores LDLR and TCR function → Enhanced T cell-mediated antitumor response → Synergy with PD-1 blockade in HCC.
Hypothesis: In hepatocellular carcinoma, inhibiting PCSK9 will restore LDLR-mediated TCR recycling on CD8+ T cells and enhance their activation, thereby synergizing with PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors to produce a more robust antitumor immune response.
Abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a challenging malignancy in part due to an immune‐suppressive tumor microenvironment that limits T cell mediated clearance. Emerging evidence indicates that PCSK9, a key regulator of low‐density lipoprotein receptor (LDLR) degradation, also modulates T cell receptor (TCR) recycling and subsequent T cell activation. Elevated PCSK9 in HCC may reduce LDLR availability on T cells, leading to impaired TCR recycling and attenuated anti‐tumor responses. This hypothesis suggests that inhibition of PCSK9 will restore LDLR function, improve TCR recycling, and enhance CD8+ T cell activity. In addition, combining PCSK9 blockade with immune checkpoint inhibitors such as PD‐1/PD‐L1 antibodies may further amplify anti‐tumor immunity in HCC.
